limitations: This optional experimental Rust analyzer patch is not applied by the default vendor or public library.

The precheck covers direct integer DIV projections with a literal NULL numerator and a strict numeric-column cast chain as divisor over locally evaluable VALUES. It does not provide general Spark expression evaluation.

The 24 preceding corpora retain 172 value/type/coarse-stage differences. The new 588 observations retain 20: eight conditional/NULL-parent observations and twelve DOUBLE/Decimal filter-coercion observations. Repeated widths, ANSI modes and shapes are observations, not independent bugs.
Five older cause gaps, four empty-subquery cause gaps and four new filter-coercion cause gaps remain separate from the coarse comparator. Four wrapped-sort diagnostics are also retained.
The floating BIGINT endpoint adjustment uses native CASE only in a discarded local precheck after native evaluation fails. Ordinary runtime numeric CAST compatibility is unchanged.

Only ten benchmark scenarios were timed. Large VALUES inputs, the failed-cast/endpoint retry, Delta I/O and concurrent workloads were not timed separately. Identical physical plans do not establish zero overhead.
The timing and code-generation evidence is specific to the recorded Rust 1.97.1 build and this host; it is not a guarantee for every compiler or CPU.
